title: Was great until it wasn’t
body:
I’ve been using this app for over a year to plan budgets, meal planning, organize events and much more. It literally saved my sanity being able to have everything I needed close and organized. I loved all the tools and ways I could customize and organize all of my notes. I used this app DAILY. 
Suddenly one day the app started crashing. I would open the app and get into the note and before I could even write anything it shut down. Sometimes it would barely get to the main screen before, poof! It was gone. I have tried so much from force quitting and restarting. Power cycling my iPad. Off loading and redownloading the app. Deleting EVERYTHING, every file, folder, note… and then uninstalling and re downloading. And still crash after crash.
I have been battling this for a couple of weeks now And it’s made the app literally unusable. I will keep it downloaded a little longer or until my subscription is set to renew to give them time to fix it but I fear it is time for me to try to find another app.

body:
Warning, this updated app is currently unusable if you ever cut/paste. It crashes infinitely, and the worst part is that you forever lose whatever you cut, because you’re never able to paste it again since it crashes every time. This has now been two major “updates” this year that have broken fundamental parts of the app. The last time it was fixed over time, but these major flaws seem like things that should be caught easily during testing before pushing out an update that bricks core functionality pieces of the app.

title: Still my favorite after all these years 🤍
body:
I don’t usually write reviews, but I’ve been using Goodnotes for about five years now and I just felt like I should finally leave one.

I’m an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery resident, so I spend a ridiculous amount of time with huge textbooks, PDFs, notes, highlighting, writing all over pages, making study plans… basically half of my academic life is inside this app 😭 I even use it for random everyday lists and things I need to remember.

I’ve tried other note-taking apps over the years, especially when I kept seeing them advertised everywhere. I’ve even paid for subscriptions just because I wanted to properly try them and see if I was missing something. And some of them are genuinely good.

But I always end up back on Goodnotes.

I don’t even know how to explain it properly anymore. It just feels like my app. I know where everything is, writing feels natural, studying feels natural, and after using it for so many years I honestly find it difficult to study on anything else.

There are always new apps and new features being advertised, but Goodnotes has been there through years of residency, exams, textbooks, stressful study nights, random notes, plans… everything.

So this is mostly just a thank you to the people behind it. 🤍 You made something I genuinely use almost every single day of my life, and I think sometimes we forget how much work must go into keeping an app like this running and improving for years.

Still my go-to. Still five stars. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

title: Infuriating update!
body:
I’ve been using this note-taking app for quite some time now. While it has always lacked a few creative features—like a lasso tool to flip objects horizontally or vertically and other tools that are common in similar apps—I still chose to stick with it because of its simplicity and the freedom it gave me when writing, drawing, or organizing my files. However, this new update, although maybe well intentioned, has taken away a lot of that freedom and has made the app frustrating to use.

For example, when I draw a straight line and hold it to keep it clean, it randomly transforms into an infinity symbol or some other unwanted shape. When I draw a triangle and want to erase part of a line or remove the fill inside, that’s no longer possible without constantly going into shape settings and adjusting options every single time I want a different triangle. This becomes a hassle, especially because I work with math every day—drawing graphs, sketching diagrams, and writing equations—so I need quick and precise control, not extra steps.

Also, another infuriating issue I’ve run into is when I try to draw a simple diagonal line while holding to make it straight snd clean. For some reason, the app automatically bends the line into a 90-degree angle instead of leaving it diagonal like I intended. If there is a way to turn off this “auto-correction,” it is extremely difficult to find. I’ve searched through the settings with no luck, and it shouldn’t be this hard to disable something so basic. Simply selecting a line to make it longer is becomes infuriating.

On top of all this, I can’t even switch back to the previous version of the app, which is really disappointing because I preferred how it worked before. To give credit where it’s due, I still really like the file system—it’s easy to save, organize, and import files, which I appreciate. But I honestly wish I could return to the previous version or at least turn off these forced shape edits. Some new features would be nice, sure—but not at the cost of usability.

I feel I have less freedom than I did before. As if I’m forced to take notes or draw a certain way and not how I prefer.
developer_response: We appreciate you taking the time to share your thoughts with us. It sounds like the recent update has significantly impacted your experience, and we truly value your feedback regarding the changes to the app's functionality. Your concerns about the drawing tools, particularly the unexpected transformations when trying to create shapes and lines, are important for us to hear. We recognize how essential precise control and ease of use are, especially for tasks like drawing graphs and sketching diagrams in your daily work with math. title: Could be great but it’s kinda mid
body:
This app was great until they decided to shove AI into everything.

The worst part isn’t even the AI itself—it’s the complete lack of transparency around AI credits. You’re not clearly told when you’re using them, what exactly is consuming them, or how many credits an action costs. You basically have to use the app and hope you don’t unknowingly burn through your allowance.

It feels less like a useful feature and more like a carefully designed subscription trap: make the credit system confusing, let users run out, then conveniently offer them a way to pay more.

Goodnotes used to feel like a genuinely great productivity app. Now it feels like another company desperately trying to monetize AI whether users asked for it or not.

Capitalism strikes again. What a shame.

body:
The note-taking app 
itself is fine, but the backend account system is terrible.

I already paid for a Goodnotes subscription through Apple, but because of an old account association, Goodnotes prevents me from properly using my purchase or subscribing with my current account. Reinstalling the app does nothing because this is clearly an account-side/backend issue.

What makes it worse is the support. Their AI bot told me to reply “human human” to reach a real support agent. I requested a human on September 3 and again on September 6. It is now September 9 and I still haven’t received meaningful help from a human.

A paid productivity app should not have an account and purchase system this unreliable. The backend service and customer support are extremely frustrating.

title: Nonexistent customer service
body:
The app itself is not bad, but if you need customer support for any reason, simply forget about it. I have been a long-time paying customer of Goodnotes since 2020; bought Goodnotes 5, and even the ridiculous Goodnotes 6 special edition. I finally needed help with something after 6 years of using it, because it was still not working after reading all the support FAQs and articles. But unfortunately, their definition of “support” is ignoring every email until you give up. I have sent in-app tickets, submitted requests from the website, emailed them multiple times over weeks, to no avail. The least they could do, even if they can’t address my concerns right away, is an acknowledgement of my email. But nah, they don’t even care enough to automate that. And apparently it is a common issue. Very disappointing, and I will not be purchasing any future versions.
Update: Goodnotes responded to this review saying I should contact support for assistance. BUT AS I KEPT SAYING, THEY DO NOT RESPOND! MULTIPLE *DETAILED* REQUESTS OVER WEEKS!! It’s almost as if they’re mocking the content of my review. The disrespect is appalling. I’m incredibly disappointed beyond words.

title: Honestly kind of trash.
body:
I really wanted to like Goodnotes, but the app feels unnecessarily complex and frustrating to use compared with other note-taking apps.

Basic functions are buried behind menus and settings that are not intuitive, and the learning curve for simple things like scrolling, selecting text, highlighting, and syncing is way higher than it should be.

The cloud syncing has also been disappointing. I imported a very small PDF on my computer and it sat with a spinning cloud for several minutes, while the same note appeared on my iPad with completely blank pages. For an app that is supposed to work seamlessly across Apple devices, syncing should not feel this unreliable or slow.

The highlighting experience is another major frustration. If I want a clean text-based highlight with proper square borders around the words, I have to hold down on the text with my finger and manually select it. I cannot simply use the Apple Pencil to select the printed text in the same way. Using the Apple Pencil highlighter instead just creates a drawn stroke, which does not give the same clean, precise borders around the actual text.

For an app designed around iPad and Apple Pencil note-taking, having to constantly switch between the Pencil and my finger for basic text selection feels poorly thought out.

There are definitely a lot of features in Goodnotes, but that is also part of the problem. The app feels overcomplicated rather than intuitive. Simple tasks require too many steps, syncing feels inconsistent, and the Apple Pencil experience is more limited than I expected.

I switched because I wanted a better note-taking experience, but so far Goodnotes has made basic tasks feel more difficult than they need to be. A note-taking app should make studying faster and easier, not make users spend time figuring out how to perform basic functions.
developer_response: Hello! Thank you for your review and feedback. We're sorry for the experience you've had with Goodnotes. It's disheartening to hear about the challenges you've faced with the app's complexity, syncing issues, and highlighting process. Your insights are invaluable and help us understand where improvements are needed. Our goal is to create a seamless experience, especially with Apple devices, and we regret that it hasn't met your expectations. For further assistance, please contact us at https://support.goodnotes.com/hc/en-us/requests/new. Thank you again for sharing your thoughts!

title: MY EXPERIENCES
body: Goodnotes has helped me a lot with studying and note taking while I was completing my AAS, the unlimited amount of notes after the lifetime subscription let me take as many notes as I wanted and store PDF from my classes. My only disappointment is the limit of pictures that I can upload at a time, since I wanted to save captures of practice questions sets from a page that my program gave me and my classmates to study for our VTNE exam. I took the screenshots of the non-math questions with the object to upload them at Goodnotes so I could transcribe them later, but when I went to start transcribing to my surprise only 6 of the almost hundred of pictures per domain I took were uploaded; making me lose study materials since I trusted that every single screenshot would be uploaded. Now I’m stock with little study materials and have to figure out a way to find new materials to study for my VTNE that’s on September 24th. It would be great if there’s not a limit to how many pictures you can upload at a time, this way users won’t have to worry about deleting screenshots from study resources from their device to free space in their device. That’s the only reason why I don’t give the app 5 stars.

title: Can’t Even Test the Free Version Before Subscribing
body:
I am trying to test Goodnotes before committing to a subscription, but every time I try to open a new notebook, I get the message, “Empty your trash bin to make sure deleted notebooks aren't counting towards your quota, or upgrade for unlimited notebooks.”

The problem is that I have zero notebooks (or anything else) in my account, and I cannot find the trash bin anywhere in the app. I went to the Goodnotes support site for help, which says, “Head to the Library view, tap the Menu icon in the top-right corner, and select Trash.” However, every time I click on “Library” in the menu bar (it is not listed in the sidebar), nothing happens. It is as if my account does not even have access to the Library option.

I don't know whether this is a glitch that is incorrectly telling me to delete notebooks that don't exist or whether the free version is intentionally so restrictive that it pushes users toward subscribing before they can properly try the app. Either way, I am not going to invest in a subscription for something that is already causing problems before I have even had the chance to test it.

title: Cornell Template Cues Column Way Too Small
body:
First, I love Good Notes and think it’s by far the best note taking app. However, I very rarely use it for one reason. I primarily write notes in Cornell style. While it’s nice Good Notes has a template for this, it’s incredibly frustrating to see how tiny the Cues column is. You’d be lucky to fit two words. I’m sure there was some reason that size was selected, but the fact there is no way to adjust the size is extremely frustrating. For me, it needs to be moved over a full inch for me to feel comfortable using it.

The writing capabilities of Good Notes is unmatched, but since there’s not a convenient way to take notes how I prefer, I will still probably rarely to ever use it and will continue using One Note. It’s far from perfect, but I can at least do Cornell notes comfortably on it.

title: Don’t waste your money - Bait-and-switch: Essentials Won’t sync between iOS and Android
body:
The entire reason I purchased GoodNotes is to do sync across all the devices in my ecosystem.  Unfortunately, the reasonably priced “Essentials” tier at $12/year locks you to sync only within the IOS Ecosystem, and won’t cross-sync to Android devices.  Annoyingly, it won’t sync web content across those two ecosystems either. If you sign in with an ID used on ios, it will HIDE web content created on PC or Android. They had to go do active development specifically to BREAK sync to force you into a higher-cost plan. 
You have to upgrade to the $36/year “Pro” plan to allow cross-device sync.  
This is a terrible bait-and-switch - when I first tried GoodNotes, they claimed a “paid subscription” would be required to enable cross-device sync.  “Essentials” is paid, but won’t do the job.  Nobody should be wasting their money on this app as a trial: expect further erosion of capabilities, now that they’ve figured out how to game their user base into paying more for a feature that should be a baseline capability.  When Onyx, OneNote, and Notion can do this at their free tiers, there’s no reason to use GoodNotes. 
In addition, the sync logic is buggy, causes data loss, and isn’t workable with an intermittent internet connection.  
Undocumented bug: GoodNotes requires a full-time, full-bandwidth connection to the internet _at all times_: it’s a wrapper around the web service, with no ability to edit/update/display/store a local replica for note taking when you’re in an area with marginal internet, and no cellular coverage (like many lecture halls and engineering spaces, the places that I NEED to take notes in) 
I you open a notebook with marginal internet, it’ll just spin for minutes until it downloads a fresh copy of your cloud save, and will then be subject to random freezes and stalls as the app attempts to sync the entire thing regularly.  Recording continuously under these conditions is also impossible, so don’t think you can record the lecture, then listen later and update your notes - nope, the recording is corrupted and intermittent, too.  Don’t waste your money evaluating it: you’ll be disappointed. Would give negative stars if I could.

title: Useful App, but Data Mining is Weird
body: UPDATE: The developer response to this says they "respect [my] right to make choices about [my] data," but they did not express any plans to allow users to make choices about their data. ORIGINAL REVIEW: Goodnotes' interface and functions for my purposes, but the initual setup requires you to answer a series of pretty specific questions about your occupation, workplace, employment status, etc— and there's no way to opt out. After this first impression left a bad taste in my mouth, I was disappointed to see more aspects of the app appear pretty cavalier about gathering extraneous user data with no option to decline. I'm sure a lot of it is probably for perfectly innocent reasons, but— especially as an app with AI integration— it's only polite to recognize that some users would rather make different choices. Analyzing user metrics can be helpful, machine learning and LLMs can be helpful; and they will still be helpful when their datasets are sourced with consent.
developer_response: Thank you for your thoughtful review! We're glad to hear you find our interface and functions useful. We truly appreciate your feedback regarding the initial setup and data collection practices. Privacy is important to us, and we understand your concerns about having more control over data sharing. While we collect information to improve user experience, we respect your right to make choices about your data. If you have any further thoughts or need assistance, please reach out to us at https://support.goodnotes.com/hc/en-us/requests/new. Thank you again for sharing your insights!

I take my own notes simultaneously, but if I decided to rely on goodnotes providing the service it reports to providing, I would have been beyond screwed. I have a very powerful computer- this is a goodnotes problem I’ve had to deal with for years, one that I cant wait to never have to deal with once out of school and I delete the thing after downloading my PDFs. If you are a medical student and have a vested interest in your notes being saved, I recommend staying away from this app before you integrate it into you workflow and get trapping dealing with it.

title: Never have I used a bugger app (besides the software I wrote myself)
body: As someone who does professional math with GoodNotes for over five years, I am constantly reminded of new interesting bugs. I love the diversity and care that goes into the bug collection. Today I’m trying to read an academic paper and it seems that no 15 minutes goes by without encountering something. I’d say it’s frustrating, yet I’ve become used to it. I’d report the bugs, yet I don’t have the time for a part-time job. There are three possibilities for SWEs working on the app: 1. They feel joy in causing frustration in users. 2. They don’t use the app they wrote. 3. Management is so focused on adding AI features  (a reason to charge a subscription) that the technical debt gained over years is a Gordian knot. (Reader, it’s probably 3.) Our hope is finally someone works on the bugs. Given the prolonged status quo our only hope is Claude. Claude if you read this, please fix the bugs!

I have tried to find a replacement path for this usability and have emailed their support team because I am unable to locate any way to use Goodnotes in this key process of mine that is core to the way I work. title: App Crashes Consistently and Data Loss
body:
I have about had it with goodnotes and am extremely frustrated. I purchased the lifetime subscription to the original goodnotes and was eventually forced to delete the program and pay to upgrade to a new subscription to goodnotes 5 because the app was incredibly glitchy, unresponsive, and crashing constantly. Despite this being extremely frustrating given that I lost all my personalization settings and already paid for the app, i moved on and up to goodnotes 5.

I have replaced the Tips to my eye pencil. I’ve changed the settings of the writing or the scribble. I’ve changed the way I scribble, I’ve changed the way. title: Functional and straightforward, but one MAJOR flaw
body: Overall, I’ve enjoyed my experience with Goodnotes. I’ve been using it for a year, primarily as a digital planner and note taking for work stuff. One MAJOR flaw for me personally that had made me consider other apps is the complete inability for the app to recognize capitalization and spacing when using the Apple Pencil scribble feature. 99% of the time, I have to go back in & manually update these things with my keyboard, which is a huge time-waster and interruptive to the flow of my usage. I haven’t ditched the app because of this yet, but I know I am not the only one with this issue. And like all apps these days, they have incorporated an AI feature. I have not used it, but if they are able to prioritize these types of updates, you would think they would address this, considering it has been an issue for YEARS according to my findings when looking for solutions. I do like the app, the templates available & overall functionality. But this is a MAJOR drawback that will become the reason I ditch Goodnotes eventually if it is not fixed.

title: Poor Pen Performance
body: I was a long-time Goodnotes user with the prior version on my M1 iPad Pro.  That was a fantastic experience and I routinely used the app for marking up pdfs, signing things, and regular bullet journaling.  I recently updated to an M4 iPad Pro/Pencil Pro and this new version of Goodnotes and I’m honestly frustrated.  The pen performance is not as good.  I write quickly and the pen engine (or whatever is translating my input) in this new version routinely leaves small tails on my letters and inputs that I did not intend unless I stop the pen fully before pulling off the screen.  From doing some research it appears this has something to do with the prediction built in to the software?  I’ve tried everything I can find: “reduce latency” is on, stroke stabilization low or off,  different palm rejection settings, etc.  Nothing changes the underlying problem which is that the app requires you to write more slowly than I do in order to have neat endings without phantom strokes being put on the page.  This is disappointing and I have ended up using the Apple Notes app for more things now as a result.  If anything can be done on this, fast writers like me would greatly appreciate it.  The rest of the app is fine.  AI note taking didn’t work that well for me, but I never used it for that sort of thing.  I didn’t even really want to buy the new app, but got tired of the nagging prompts and decided to “upgrade” with my new iPad.  I wish I hadn’t.
developer_response: Thank you for your review and for sharing your experience with the pen performance in the new version. It’s clear that the transition from your M1 iPad Pro to the M4 has been frustrating, especially after such a fantastic experience with the previous version. We truly appreciate you detailing the issues with unintended strokes and the adjustments you've made, like changing the latency and stroke stabilization settings. Your feedback about needing to write more slowly for neat endings is crucial, and we understand how this can be a significant adjustment for fast writers like you. It’s completely understandable that this has led you to explore other apps, and we value your insights on how we can improve in this area. We’re pleased to hear that you find the rest of the app satisfactory. If you’d like assistance or have further concerns, please feel free to reach out to us at https://support.goodnotes.com/hc/en-us/requests/new. Thank you again for sharing your thoughts, and we hope you continue to find joy in your note-taking journey!

title: Too many unnecessary “features”
body:
I got this app because my classmates used it, and it started good. 

But over time I noticed these unnecessary “features” that annoyed me. 

When I tap the 4 squares to show all pages in a list, goodnotes will start at the top then scroll down to the page i’m currently on. This is cool and all, but it’s a good half second delay each time i press the button to find a page. Please, just give me the page I’m on. 

I also like to organize my notes in folders and subfolders; but every time I open a folder there’s another half second delay while I wait for the contents to slide in from the side of the screen. Maybe this is just to hide the loading time of the files, but it’s just file browsing, it shouldn’t even need to have a delay. If it’s not, please get rid of this animation and just show me my goddamn notes. 

What made me write this review:

After updating to the latest iOS, a new bug appeared. Every time I switch tabs between 2 different files, Goodnotes will scroll me up to the top of the page. But if i’m already there, it will scroll me up to the previous page. Literally nobody asked for this; I can scroll my own damn screen. This bug apparently was found 7 months ago online and it still isn’t fixed.

Please Goodnotes, stop implementing these bloated animations and features that only waste time and interfere with actual note taking.

title: Below average for PDF markups
body:
I had a consistently frustrating experience using the app for PDF markup.

Handwriting input was especially difficult to use well. It was inaccurate in ways that created constant friction rather than speeding anything up. A clear example was the app repeatedly converting a capital “I” into the number “1.” Errors like that were surprisingly hard to correct cleanly without giving up and switching to the keyboard, which disrupted the whole workflow. Instead of feeling like a smooth handwriting-first experience, it often felt like I was fighting the recognition and cleanup process just to produce basic, readable notes.

Separately, the comment tool does not export reliably. Even when using typed comments and selecting the correct export settings, including flattened PDF with comments enabled, the comments fail to appear in standard PDF viewers. This makes the feature unsuitable for sharing or submitting annotated documents.

Overall, the app does not provide a dependable workflow for creating and exporting annotated PDFs, particularly when the output must be viewed outside the app.
developer_response: Hello! Thank you for your review and feedback. We're sorry for the experience you've had with the app for PDF markup. It sounds like you've encountered some significant challenges, particularly with handwriting recognition and the comment tool. The confusion between letters and numbers can certainly disrupt your workflow, and we recognize how important it is for the app to provide a seamless handwriting experience. title: Time for a CLASS ACTION LAWSUIT?!?!
body:
1.  I paid for an app that is now refusing to sync between my iPhone and iPad and will only load on my iPhone (regardless of the fact that I originally purchased on my iPad) making my iPad app, and Apple Pencil, useless even though I am signed into all cloud services properly.  Help searches state that due to having purchased a lifetime, one-time, premium version of this app, I would need to pay for a subscription payment plan to be able to sync between devices.  The partial content, that is loaded on my iPad is incomplete or corrupted. 

2.  I have spent countless hours on the phone with my internet provider tying to resolve the syncing errors (that are made to appear as internet connection errors by the app) only to be told it is an issue with apples new iOS or the app. I have then spent hours with Apple support to be told it is an app specific issue. 

3.  Next, emails to support from both devices have gone unanswered.  Not to mention, of the numerous reviews read, I have not read even one updated review stating that this company has rectified this situation or made anyone whole. Worse yet, all responses seem heavily AI created, showcasing the lack of customer support. 

4.  Heavily relying brand recognition, positive reviews over an extended period of time, the guarantee of a one-time purchase of a lifetime subscription of this app, and the ability to keep and save everything on device as well as the ability to backup everything to iCloud…I felt confident and comfortable enough to import and create numerous documents and notebooks and make this my only source/app for everything in my life, including sensitive medical information, family information and time-sensitive work projects. 

5.  Still holding out hope that there would be a new update or fix or the ability to migrate back to the working/previous version that was purchased, I came here to check, prior to updating again, decided to read the 100’s of reviews stating the same issues and have lost any hope that this massive fraud, greed and corruption would be rectified.  

6.  I refuse to pay an endless subscription to an app I already purchased the rights to use with no additional cost, and especially an app with no ability to disable the AI features that will undoubtedly “learn from’’ and compromise my extremely sensitive content as I would never have purchased an app that did not have the ability to disable that feature.  Not to mention, of the numerous reviews read, I have not read even one updated review stating that this company has rectified this situation or made anyone whole. Worse yet, all responses seem heavily AI created, showcasing the lack of customer support. 

7.  The amount of time lost, medical health compromised, family member’s scholarships affected/lost, reputation lost (due to recommending this app to numerous work partners and others…almost all with the same issues), work lost, and financial loss due t o this fraud makes the case for not letting this drop at just migrating to a new app and leaving a negative review.  Especially due to the fact that I am disabled and heavily relied on this app for every aspect of my life. 

8.  I assume I will be getting a chat bot tailored response to this review apologizing and asking me to contact them, even though they couldn’t respond to any previous emails…and at that point, I will give one chance for them to respond and make this right within 3 business days of receiving a copy of this review. Should they do what is right, I will delete this review. If they choose otherwise,  I feel launching a public campaign exposing this predatory behavior to warn potential new people considering downloading this app or advertisers considering partnering with this app, filing a complaint with Apple, filing complaints with all governing consumer protection bodies will be the the first step then possibly proceeding to a class-action lawsuit.

I hope this review helped and have a great day! 


Response to developer:

In the interest of transparency, and for those following due to similar issues, I am posting my response here.

I assure you, and will restate and cannot emphasize enough, I have tried every single fix posted from your community/Reddit/YouTube/Apple/AT&T/internet searches, etc., including the most obvious fix, which your reply suggested confirming, I am logged into the correct account on each device. In my case, it is my Apple ID. All settings are identical on both devices. The only difference between devices is the blue “sync now” button which is a dead click/non-functional button, which shows the last back up being April 2025! I hope that information helps you understand how long this issue has been going on.  

I will wait for your reply so that this additional information can “sync” in (pun intended) and help you figure out your problem prior to contacting Support again as I have no faith this will be resolved outside of this review. I do appreciate you confirming that this should not be a problem.
developer_response: Thank you for your follow-up. We hear you, this is clearly not a login mismatch issue. Special Edition plan fully supports iCloud sync between Apple devices. Please email us at support@goodnotes.com mentioning this review and include Diagnostic Data from both devices, as this will provide more necessary details for our investigation. We are committed to resolving this promptly.

title: High Cognitive Load Failure
body:
Goodnotes may look polished, but it fails in core usability. Organization is unintuitive, essential tools like text input are not readily available, and navigation relies on hidden or inconsistent menus.

For users who need to quickly capture, paste, and format information, the app creates unnecessary friction instead of supporting the workflow. Basic actions should not require customization or workarounds.

A notes app should prioritize clarity, accessibility, and speed. In its current state, Goodnotes falls short in all three.

I wrote down a 0 amongst other things while planning my day and it let me erase everything else except the 0. Even when I refreshed the app, it was still unable to erase. On top of that, it wouldn’t even let me cover it up with the background color! Or any color, it would just delete the drawing. But when it came to its own color, it let it stay? Confusing, weird, and just frustrating when I’m just trying to plan out my day. On top of that, the text box function changed and it feels like the app is constantly on its first day at its first job. What makes a good app is its ability to perform and Goodnotes is a good app, but it could be better. Like, so much better. Not out of any malice I do I say any of this, I wanna keep using this app but using the functions is a true test to my ability to be peaceful. This issue may have to do with the app’s use of AI (Yall never needed no AI, it is just unnecessary.), along with many other issues. I want to keep using the app, so please fix these issues, thank you.

title: Screwed up the Fundamentals
body:
If I move a chunk of text, I can no longer erase any part of it. Seriously, how do you get an eraser wrong? It also does janky things like auto switching to the eraser after switching from the select tool. 
Furthermore, it has a frustrating algorithm for the hold and release shapes. Good luck trying to draw mathematical diagrams, your lines will lock to places you don’t want them to, and the new updates makes it highly impractical to edit shapes. 
Indeed, since I’ve been using it, it’s gone downhill. Just look into the Goodnotes Reddit forum to see examples. 
The short of it is that Goodnotes 7 consumes more battery life than ever, as it is bloated with unused features, and the most basic tools are becoming less and less reliable. I feel very ripped off for paying for this, free options provide a better day to day experience. Save your time and use Noteful or something, I would refund if I could.

- UPDATE -
Changed from 3 to 4 stars. 
It seems Goodnotes 7 was pushed too soon, but they largely ironed out those issues. I still would prefer more streamline functionality to preserve battery life. AI tools? Really don’t need them. One thing they haven’t gotten down is the pen-based lasso tool. That is, where you circle something with the pen and then click and hold to create a lasso selection of that shape.

body:
GoodNotes has a clean, thoughtfully designed interface that makes it easy to capture and organize ideas. There’s also a low learning curve, so it doesn’t take long to start using it quickly and effectively.

I especially like the built-in marketplace for templates while I’ve found some of the more unique or higher-quality options on Etsy, the convenience of having templates directly within the app is a strong plus.

Overall, it’s a great tool for how I use it: getting thoughts out of my head and onto paper. Whether I’m planning goals, journaling, mapping out processes, or building journey maps for work, it supports that flow really well.

The one feature I’d love to see added is the ability to lock individual notes for privacy. That would make it a more complete solution, especially for users who keep both personal and professional content in the same space.
developer_response: Hello! Thank you for your thoughtful review and feedback. It's wonderful to hear how the design and ease of use enhance your note-taking experience! We genuinely appreciate your thoughts on the template marketplace and how it supports your workflow. Your suggestion about the ability to lock individual notes for privacy is valuable, and we encourage you to share it with us through our Suggestions Portal at http://feedback.goodnotes.com. For further assistance, please contact us at https://support.goodnotes.com/hc/en-us/requests/new. Thank you once again for sharing your ideas, and we're glad the app serves you well in your various tasks!

developer_response: Thank you for your review! It’s clear how important it is for you to have control over your notes, and we appreciate you sharing your experience with us. The unexpected substitutions can be quite disruptive, especially when you're trying to capture your thoughts accurately. Your suggestion to underline potentially misspelled words instead of automatically correcting them is a valuable insight. For further assistance, please feel free to reach out to us at https://support.goodnotes.com/hc/en-us/requests/new. We truly value your feedback as it helps us understand user preferences better. i reset my ipad to a backup when i had downloaded the app but hadn’t written a note in it, and then the ipad started sleeping again after 2 minutes of inactivity. but after i used goodnotes again — i just typed some lists on a page — the ipad wouldn’t go to sleep again. i deleted the app completely and restarted the ipad. the ipad is working fine again now.

additionally, i didn’t like how simple features were missing like snapping to grid, align selected elements, or even indenting bullet points. how can a note-taking app be unable to create a basic outline?

i won’t miss this app.

title: One time purchase (*fixed)
body:
I purchased goodnotes premium Feb 2025, however as of June 2025 my premium access has somehow been lost within a few months, I contacted customer support through their only form of contact (email) and have been sending back and forth emails for the past 3 WEEKS, it should not be taking this long, I am currently taking a summer course and my midterm is approaching, I have been heavily reliant on goodnotes premium and when it actually was accessible to me through my one time purchase it was great! But the stress and time that I have been devoting has been insane, as such a popular app there should definitely be much better customer service, I was hoping to love this app and honestly I did, but the customer service needs some real work and being that this is an app used by students there should not be any difficulties regarding the one time purchase since many people probably invest in it. Also as a student I already do not have that much time, I am beyond disappointed with goodnotes. (Also all of the cute stickers/ templates must be purchased if you do not make custom ones. )

Update: after 3 weeks they were able to restore my membership but it took much longer than it should have, I didn’t even have goodnotes for a year at the point of that happening.

title: Lifetime access
body:
I purchased the lifetime access promotion expecting that it would include the core features of the app moving forward. Unfortunately, I was disappointed to learn that the newly integrated AI feature now requires an additional $35 per year for 525 credits.

This was not clearly communicated during the lifetime promotion, and it feels misleading. When customers purchase “lifetime access,” there is a reasonable expectation that major new features added to the platform will be included.

I understand that apps evolve and add new technology, but transparency is important. Clear disclaimers about future paid upgrades would help customers make more informed decisions.

At the moment, it feels frustrating to have already paid for lifetime access but still be required to pay additional fees to use significant new functionality.

title: Was great, now practically unusable. AVOID if you are a med/vet student
body: I’ve been using goodnotes since undergrad (now a 3rd year vet student), and it was excellent, but in the past year, every update has been clunkier and less intuitive, and the app itself is now unusably slow. I’m talking 45-90 seconds to load a handwritten to do list. A minute between opening a folder and even a single slide deck in it will load (and all the while there’s a message displayed saying “this folder is empty”…. just enough time for the paranoia to set in that this POS app has finally gone ahead and deleted my last 7 years of work.) Apparently the files I have are all now “too large” (including my 1 page long handwritten to do list apparently) despite not being noticeably bigger than anything I’ve had on there for the past 3 years. I would suggest that if your app can’t handle “large files” then don’t market it to people training to be doctors. We tend to use a lot of those. The ONLY reason I’m still using this app is because I have just weeks left of classes before clinics and want all my notes in one place.   Please spare yourself this nightmare and treat yourself to a note taking app that doesn’t load like it’s using dial up.

title: Glitch/Tech error discovered
body:
I genuinely love Goodnotes, have used it from undergrad and even now in medical school. However, I discovered a glitch in the app. 

If you follow these steps you will see it too. 
1. Use the “Tape” feature (to cover/hide some text or content).
2. Use the eraser to erase it (as if you made an honest mistake)
3. Switch back to the pen from eraser, and try using the tape again, the app then times out/closes out. 

It gets really annoying while annotating slides or studying. If the developers can find a way to fix this bug, that would be great, better yet, that would earn my five stars rating.

title: Love this app
body: This is a great app. It does everything I needed to do, I have not explored all of the features yet, but it keeps track of everything for me! I like journaling in here because on paper journals you can’t search for something and I feel like going through menopause in my fog brain. I need to remember stuff and be able to search for stuff and I love to speak to text feature however, just writing it with my Apple pen makes such a difference. You have to write stuff down. You just have to. It helps your mental health! Thank you for a great app.
developer_response: Hello! Thank you for your wonderful review and feedback. We're delighted to hear that the app is helping you stay organized and supports your journaling needs! It's fantastic that you're enjoying the search functionality and writing with your Apple pen, as we believe writing can truly enhance mental well-being.
